title: The Ship That Watched Titanic Sink
sources: Wikipedia / Encyclopedia Titanica, 'SS Californian': stopped in an ice field the night of 14-15 April 1912; officers saw rockets; no action taken
Wikipedia, 'Cyril Furmstone Evans': Californian's wireless operator switched off his set and went to bed before Titanic's distress calls
Wikipedia, 'Stanley Lord': awakened twice and told about the rockets; replied they may be 'company rockets'
British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry report (titanicinquiry.org): officers of Californian saw eight white rockets
US Senate and British inquiries: many or all of the lives lost could have been saved had Californian responded (Wikipedia, SS Californian)
GG Archives / Wikipedia: Lord defended his actions for the rest of his life (died 1962); MAIB reappraisal 1992 - debate continues
titanicinquiry.org / greatships.net: Carpathia raced 58 miles through an ice field, arrived about 4 a.m., rescued 705 survivors

lines.text: April 1912,
the Titanic is sinking,
and she's firing rockets into the sky,
begging for help.
And here's the haunting part:
another ship could actually see them.
See, the Californian had stopped for the night,
trapped in the same field of ice,
and her radio operator had just switched off
and gone to bed.
So when her crew spotted eight white rockets,
lines.caps: So when | her crew | spotted | 8~eight | white | rockets,

lines.text: they told the captain,
who thought they might just be company signals,
and went back to sleep.
By morning, the Titanic was gone,
and more than fifteen hundred people had died.
lines.caps: and | more than | 1,500~fifteen | people | had died.

lines.text: Another ship, the Carpathia,
raced fifty-eight miles through the ice
to save the rest.
So could the Californian have saved them?
Both inquiries said yes,
many, if not all of them.
Her captain denied it until the day he died,
and more than a hundred years later,
people still argue about it.
So... what would you have done?
